# Inserting Data Into a Table

#### Course: Learn SQL Basics

## Inserting Data Into a Table

Suppose the university has just admitted a new student, "Emma Stone". She has enrolled in the course "Discrete Structure" (Course ID: C101) with a GPA of 3.8 and a student ID of 6.

You are tasked to add her information to the Students table so that the university records her enrollment.

For such tasks, SQL provides the INSERT INTO statement, which inserts one or more rows into a table.

Let's insert a new row into the Students table.

```sql
1INSERT INTO Students (id, name, course_id, GPA)
2VALUES (6, 'Emma Stone', 'C101', 3.8);
```

When you execute the SQL query above, you won't see any immediate output because the INSERT INTO statement adds data to the database without returning a result.

To verify the newly inserted data, use a SELECT query to retrieve all entries from the table.

```sql
1SELECT * 
2FROM Students;
```

You can see that the table now has a new row.

![New Student Added to the Database](data:image/png;base64,)

On the next page, we'll carefully break down the syntax of the INSERT INTO statement to know how it works.
